title: Chuam Sculpture Park in Donghae: Korea's Hidden Sunrise Spot on the East Coast (Beginner's Guide)
html:
Most first-time visitors to Korea spend their whole trip in Seoul or Busan, so you probably haven't heard of Chuam Sculpture Park (추암조각공원) yet. It sits on a small, pine-covered hill above the East Sea in Donghae, a coastal city in Gangwon-do (the mountainous province on Korea's northeast coast). The park itself is full of quirky outdoor sculptures, but the real reason people make the trip is what's just below it: one of the most famous sunrise views in the whole country.

What's Actually at the Park

"Jogak" (조각) just means "sculpture" in Korean, and that's exactly what you'll find here — a walking trail lined with modern outdoor art, an open-air stage used for small local events, and a few shaded resting areas with benches. It's a short, easy walk, not a serious hike, so it's a good stop even if you're traveling with kids or grandparents. Along the trail there's also a quiet memorial wall built to honor the allied soldiers who fought and died nearby during the Korean War (1950–1953) — a reminder that this peaceful coastline saw real fighting less than a century ago.

Chotdaebawi: The "Candle Rock" Everyone Comes to See

Right next to the park, jutting out of the sea, is a tall, narrow rock called Chotdaebawi (촛대바위), which means "candlestick rock" — chotdae is the stand for a candle, and from the right angle the rock really does look like a candle sticking up out of the water. On a clear morning, the sun rises directly behind it and seems to balance right on top for a few seconds. It's such a well-known sunrise image in Korea that it was used in the opening scene of the national anthem video shown on Korean TV. Photographers and early risers from all over the country travel here just for this one shot, so if you want a photo without a crowd of tripods in the frame, arrive at least 20–30 minutes before sunrise.

💡 Local tip: Korean photographers check the sunrise time online the night before and set an alarm — there's no trick to it beyond showing up early and picking a clear-weather day. Any Korean sunrise-time app or a quick search for "Donghae sunrise time" the night before will do the job.

Suspension Bridge, Brother Rocks, and the Legend of General Isabu

From the sculpture park, a path leads down to the Chuam Suspension Bridge, a see-through walking bridge strung between the rocks right above the waves — it sways gently as you cross, which is half the fun (and slightly nerve-wracking if you're not a fan of heights). Nearby you'll also spot Hyeongjebawi ("Brother Rocks"), a pair of rock formations said to look like two siblings standing side by side, and small lion-shaped statues connected to General Isabu, a Korean military commander from about 1,500 years ago. According to legend, Isabu mounted wooden lion statues on his ships to scare a nearby island kingdom into surrendering without a fight — a clever, bloodless trick that locals still like to tell visitors about today.

Practical Info & Getting There

The park itself is open 9:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. (extended to 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. in summer), though the beach and rock area around it are accessible any time — which is how early-morning sunrise visitors get in before the official opening hour. Admission is free, and there's a free parking lot nearby.

The easiest way to get here from Seoul is by KTX high-speed train to Donghae Station (about 2.5–3 hours), followed by a roughly 10-minute taxi ride to Chuam Beach — just show the driver "추암해변" (Chuam Beach) or "추암조각공원" on your phone. If you're coming from Gangneung or Sokcho, buses and taxis along the coast also connect easily to Donghae. For GPS, you can search "Chuam Sculpture Park" or use the coordinates 37.4790469361, 129.1586599490 in Google Maps or Naver Map.

There's no cafe or restaurant right inside the park, so it's worth grabbing coffee or breakfast in downtown Donghae before heading over, especially if you're going for sunrise.

meta_description: A beginner's guide to Chuam Sculpture Park in Donghae: Korea's famous candle-rock sunrise view, a suspension bridge, and easy KTX directions from Seoul.
